sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: In humans, since mitochondria come into the zygote only from the egg, the inheritance of mitochondrial DNA is said to be a case of ______ inheritance. Fill in the blank.
questions.answer: maternal (cytoplasmic) inheritance.

questions.q: Write the genotypes of the human blood groups: (a) A (b) AB.
questions.answer: (a) IAIA or IAi. (b) IAIB.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) A male honey bee has a father. (b) Females of birds are heterogametic.
questions.answer: (a) False. (b) True.

questions.q: Name the types of sex determination: (a) humans (b) birds.
questions.answer: (a) XX-XY type. (b) ZW-ZZ type.

questions.q: Name the chromosomal abnormality: (a) trisomy of chromosome 21 (b) XO.
questions.answer: (a) Down's syndrome. (b) Turner's syndrome.

questions.q: Match: (a) Sutton and Boveri (b) Bateson and Punnett (c) Mendel with (i) linkage (ii) chromosome theory (iii) law of segregation.
Define: (a) allele (b) genotype.
questions.answer: (a) Alternative forms of a gene at the same locus. (b) The genetic constitution of an individual.

questions.q: Give the phenotypic ratio in (a) incomplete dominance (b) test cross of a heterozygote.
questions.answer: (a) 1:2:1 (1 red : 2 pink : 1 white). (b) 1:1.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: State Mendel's law of segregation.
questions.answer: The two factors of a pair separate during gamete formation so that each gamete carries only one factor, and the gametes are pure.

questions.q: What is incomplete dominance? Give an example.
questions.answer: When neither allele is dominant and the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype; e.g. pink flowers in Mirabilis jalapa from red and white.

questions.q: Distinguish between linkage and crossing over.
questions.answer: Linkage is the tendency of genes on the same chromosome to be inherited together; crossing over is the exchange of segments between non-sister chromatids, producing recombinants.

questions.q: Explain the statement 'Male honey bees have no father but have a grandfather'.
questions.answer: Males develop from unfertilised eggs of the queen, so they have no father; they have a grandfather as the queen's father mated to produce her.

questions.q: What is pleiotropy? Give one example.
questions.answer: One gene controlling several phenotypic traits; the white eye gene in Drosophila also affects wing and abdomen shape.

questions.q: What is amniocentesis? Mention its use.
questions.answer: A technique in which amniotic fluid is withdrawn and foetal cells are cultured to detect genetic disorders; its use to find the sex of the foetus is illegal.

questions.q: Write two features of Down's syndrome.
questions.answer: Trisomy 21 (47 chromosomes), mental retardation and a thick tongue with a drooping face.

questions.q: Why do males suffer more from X-linked recessive disorders?
questions.answer: Males have only one X, so a single recessive gene is expressed; females need two.

questions.q: What is a human karyotype?
questions.answer: The arrangement of the 23 pairs of human chromosomes in seven groups A to G by size and centromere position.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: A haemophilic man marries a normal woman. Show the genotypes of both individuals. With the help of a flow chart work out the phenotype of their progeny.
questions.answer: Man: XhY; woman: XX. Gametes: Xh, Y × X, X. Progeny: XhX (carrier daughter) and XY (normal son), so all daughters are carriers and all sons are normal.

questions.q: A carrier female for red-green colour blindness marries a man with normal vision. With the help of a flow chart work out the phenotypes of the progeny.
questions.answer: Woman XCXc, man XCY; gametes XC, Xc × XC, Y; progeny XCXC (normal daughter), XCXc (carrier daughter), XCY (normal son) and XcY (colour-blind son).

questions.q: State and explain Mendel's law of independent assortment with a cross.
questions.answer: The genes of different characters assort independently. TTRR × ttrr gives TtRr in F1; F2 gives 9 tall red : 3 tall white : 3 dwarf red : 1 dwarf white.

questions.q: Describe sex determination in humans.
questions.answer: The female has XX and produces only X eggs; the male has XY and produces X and Y sperms; an X sperm gives a girl, a Y sperm gives a boy, so sex is a matter of chance.

questions.q: Explain the cause of Rh incompatibility.
questions.answer: An Rh-negative mother with an Rh-positive foetus forms antibodies against Rh antigen after the first delivery; in later pregnancies these antibodies destroy the foetal RBCs, causing erythroblastosis foetalis.

questions.q: Explain Klinefelter's and Turner's syndromes.
questions.answer: Klinefelter's: XXY male, tall, sterile with breast development; Turner's: XO female, sterile, webbed neck, underdeveloped breasts.

questions.q: Explain the inheritance of ABO blood groups.
questions.answer: Three alleles IA, IB and i; IA and IB are codominant and dominant over i; genotypes IAIA and IAi give A, IBIB and IBi give B, IAIB gives AB and ii gives O.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain Mendel's monohybrid cross and the laws it led to.
questions.answer: Tall × dwarf gives all tall F1 and 3:1 in F2; this led to the law of dominance and the law of segregation (purity of gametes); a dihybrid cross gave 9:3:3:1 and the law of independent assortment.

questions.q: Explain the chromosome theory of inheritance and linkage and crossing over.
questions.answer: Sutton and Boveri showed genes are located on chromosomes; genes on the same chromosome are linked; crossing over at chiasmata in prophase I produces recombinants.

questions.q: Explain sex-linked inheritance with reference to haemophilia and colour blindness.
questions.answer: Genes on the X chromosome show criss-cross inheritance; males are affected by a single recessive gene; carrier females pass it to half their sons; crosses with genotypes and ratios.

questions.q: Describe the deviations from Mendelian inheritance.
questions.answer: Incomplete dominance, multiple alleles and codominance, lethal genes, pleiotropy and polygenic inheritance with examples.

questions.q: Describe the chromosomal disorders and genetic diseases in humans.
questions.answer: Down's, Klinefelter's and Turner's syndromes; colour blindness, haemophilia, thalassaemia and sickle-cell anaemia.
